comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C3, C16-C22) about differential motion discrimination sensitivity between conditions. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN due to concerns about incomplete neurophysiological evidence, specifically requesting explicit mapping of saccade-related activity and better understanding of spatial configuration effects on response fields.

Both address overlapping claims about decision-related vs sensory-related components (C23-C31, C34 in OpenEval; C23-C34 in peer review). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on robust partial correlation and ROC analyses, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN due to overall concerns about incomplete neurophysiological evidence and potential confounding spatial factors, though they don't explicitly challenge these specific analyses.

Both evaluate identical claims (C37-C43) about RNN replication of neurophysiological findings. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical consistency across 50 networks with caveat about biological mechanisms, while peer reviewers explicitly identify the RNN simulations as a strength without raising concerns.

Both evaluate identical claims (C44-C46) about structured feedback connectivity emergence in RNNs. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical evidence with caveat about biological plausibility, while peer reviewers implicitly support through positive comments about RNN simulations without specific concerns.

Both evaluate identical claims (C47-C57) about in silico inactivation experiments. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive causal evidence from multiple experimental approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly identify simulated lesions as a study strength.

Both evaluate identical claims (C58-C65) about energy landscape analysis and decision consistency mechanisms. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes theoretical consistency with caveats about 1-D approximation and speculative interpretation, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic analysis without explicit criticism.

Both evaluate claim C73 about the modulation not being explained by simple gain changes. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on nonlinear modulation patterns and control analyses, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, directly challenging this interpretation due to lack of explicit evidence on response field sizes/locations and potential confounding from spatial configuration.

OpenEval evaluates claims C66-C69 about conceptual distinction from attention, rating SUPPORTED based on dissociation patterns and literature comparison. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretive claims.
